gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-dogra: Strong, tightly packed Franchise stands tall with wire-thin uniform strokes, outlines drawn in a single width. And Noto Serif Dogra, a classic serif, gives its curves a faint thick-thin rhythm where even the thinnest points keep real weight.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-ethio: Bookish and settled, Noto Serif Ethiopic forms words into solid blocks instead of jagged skylines, with only modest stroke modulation. But Franchise, with its wire-like line, is what sits above it, tall and tightly spaced.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-georg: Authoritative Noto Serif Georgian coils its lowercase tight like rope, with a slight swell on the bowls, while Franchise has no calligraphic swelling anywhere. Give the text face the larger size.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-gujar: Franchise jams its tall, narrow letters against each other, with every curve drawn without any stress at all. And Noto Serif Gujarati, a classic serif, brings oversized counters and a middling thick-thin difference that loosen things up.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-gurmu: Editorial and literary, Noto Serif Gurmukhi has a generous x-height and weight that shifts gradually, like a stretched rubber cord, only slightly. Franchise holds its stroke widths steady from stem to curve.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-hebre: Noto Serif Hebrew is a classic serif with a tall, sturdy lowercase and a mellow thick-thin difference, set against heading strokes like cut ribbon. Franchise earns its keep big and short.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-kanna: Franchise draws tubelike, constant-weight lines in tall small letters, and it does its best work in bold, compact headings. But Noto Serif Kannada, a classic serif, does its best with big counters and thin strokes just slightly lighter than the thick.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-khmer: Noto Serif Khmer reads sturdy and traditional, with tall lowercase nearly meeting the capitals. Franchise does its best work as a strong, clean heading with no calligraphic swelling, while this text serif handles moderately modulated strokes with more nuance.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-khojk: Franchise sets crossbars as thick as its stems, in tall letters pressed hard against their neighbors. It excels at that bold clarity, while Noto Serif Khojki, a text serif, adds refined short ascenders and a slight pinch.
gen-dafont-franchise-gf-noto-serif-lao: Noto Serif Lao reads bookish and authoritative, its big lowercase height towering over the capitals, with bowls shifting gently in weight. And Franchise's lines, bent like rope or tubing, make a striking counterpart to that classic serif.
